item.title: DiscoverEU applications now open: Thousands of free travel passes for young Europeans up for grabs
item.description: Applications for the scheme are open until 15 October, giving eligible young Europeans the chance to explore the continent by train and other sustainable transport, with discounts on accommodation, culture and more.

item.title: Fact check: What's going on with Spain's 'Maricarmen' housing protests?
item.description: Spanish protests against the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen have led to misleading claims about Spain's housing activists and the wider rental crisis.

item.title: Schools closed, services slowed and flights cancelled: strikes hit Portugal
item.description: Three CGTP unions have called a strike for Friday, disrupting schools, public services, councils and rubbish collection. An easyJet cabin crew walkout is also causing flight delays nationwide.

item.title: Could the future of AI data centres be in space? Google wants to find out
item.description: The tech giant has launched a prototype satellite carrying its AI chips to explore whether solar powered infrastructure in orbit could one day support large-scale computing.

item.title: European diesel reserves cover 10 days of the world's demands, expert says
item.description: "Even if all of 300 million barrels of European reserves are released, it will only cover around 10 to 11 days of the world's diesel demand", energy expert, Osama Rizvi tells Euronews and Europe Today, about President Trump's call to European countries to release some of their diesel reserves.

item.title: EU adds €130 million to drone funding in border security push
item.description: The Commission is adding €130 million for drone technology as Brussels steps up border surveillance and prepares to strengthen Frontex’s role.

item.title: Hundreds of high schools in France close as new protests against conditions erupt
item.description: The students say their school hours are excessively long, conditions inadequate including overheated classrooms, and that there are too many staff absences.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 2nd, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 2nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Meloni asks Brussels for fiscal leeway as energy shock squeezes Italy
item.description: Italian prime Minister Giorgia Meloni is urging the European Commission again to relax the EU's fiscal rules, saying that higher inflation due to soaring energy prices is squeezing households and businesses, according to a letter seen by Euronews.

item.title: Bonds steady as French borrowing costs hit 24-year high and UK 30-year yields top 6%
item.description: Government bond markets steadied on Friday morning after a sell-off pushed France's 10-year borrowing costs to their highest since 2002, lifted UK 30-year yields above 6% for the first time since 1998 and drove the benchmark US 10-year yield to a 24-year high.

item.title: Eurozone inflation spikes to 3.8%: Is your country on the worst list?
item.description: Eurozone inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, a three-year high above forecasts. Energy drove the spike. See where prices rose fastest.

item.title: New severe weather alert issued for Crete as heavy rainfall already recorded
item.description: Disruption caused by the recent bout of severe weather continues, with authorities warning that further problems may arise as conditions remain unsettled.

item.title: These are the easiest countries to be a digital nomad in, according to a new study
item.description: Holafly’s Digital Nomad Friction Index 2026 looked at factors such as visa complexity, banking access, healthcare and cost of living.

item.title: What does music look like? This British artist paints what he hears
item.description: Sounds can sometimes interrupt Andrew’s thoughts, but he sees synaesthesia as an inseparable part of his life.

item.title: Did Trump order Maduro’s kidnapping based on Grok’s advice?
item.description: The US president spent hours in the White House asking Musk’s AI chatbot questions, including how Venezuelans would react if the US captured Maduro, Time magazine reports.

item.title: Traffic gridlocked in Ukraine's capital as Russian drone strikes close key bridge
item.description: Ukraine has long feared an attack on its major transportation bridges since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

item.title: EU holds crisis meeting as US pressure mounts to release emergency oil stocks
item.description: EU countries and the European Commission are holding talks on Friday that could pave the way for a new emergency oil reserves release, as pressure from Washington mounts. Energy Commissioner Dan Jørgensen told Euronews a fresh emergency release is "a possibility".

item.title: Trans-Caspian Corridor: Europe and Central Asia target faster trade
item.description: Transit along the Trans-Caspian Corridor currently takes around 35 days, with a target of cutting this to between 15 and 20. Officials say customs, digital systems and predictable border procedures are as important as new railways and ports.

item.title: Pete Hegseth creates Pentagon Office of Religious Affairs reporting directly to him
item.description: Hegseth has infused his evangelical Christianity into his leadership of the Pentagon, hosting worship services for employees and often speaking of the United States as a Christian nation.

item.title: No silver bullet to energy crisis, EU Energy chief says
item.description: EU Energy Commissioner, Dan Jørgensen on winter storage, prices and emergency releases.

item.title: Houthis deny Saudi accusations of targeting Medina's holy sites
item.description: The Saudi-led coalition said a drone hit the Taibah electricity distribution station, which supplies power to the Prophet's Mosque, one of Islam's holiest sites. The Houthis denied the claim, stating it was a "lie" to back previous allegations against the group.

item.title: World's tallest wind turbine rises to 365 metres in Germany
item.description: Germany’s new 365-metre wind turbine in Schipkau is the world’s tallest, designed to capture stronger winds and start operating in November.

item.title: Uzbekistan wins home gold at record-breaking Chess Olympiad in Samarkand
item.description: Almost 400 teams from more than 190 countries competed over 11 rounds. Germany took bronze, while Hungary, France and Spain also finished in the top 10, alongside Azerbaijan and Armenia.

item.title: 'I was fighting for my life': FlyDubai captain recalls cockpit attack
item.description: Still recovering in hospital, the pilot who helped prevent a tragedy on a FlyDubai flight has spoken publicly about the moment he fought to regain control of the cockpit. Capt. Smit Machchhar says he was “fighting for his life” but knew he had to get back up as the aircraft began its steep descent.

item.title: Christa Pike in critical condition after Tennessee botched execution, lawyer says
item.description: Pike was 18 when she and her boyfriend beat and killed Colleen Slemmer, 19, at a job training camp for young people.

item.title: Țoiu: NATO and EU must boost response to hybrid attacks
item.description: Romania is on the front line of Europe’s security challenge.

item.title: Dual UK-Iranian national arrested over security incident at RAF air base in England
item.description: Five men, all British nationals in their 20s and from London, were arrested in the early hours of Sunday on suspicion of explosives and terror offenses close to the RAF Fairford base.

item.title: Madrid protesters bang pots to demand action on Spain’s housing crisis
item.description: Madrid demonstrators bang pots and pans to demand action on Spain’s housing crisis, calling for long‑term security and support for young adults seeking homes.

item.title: EU says oil reserve release possible amid US pressure
item.description: Good morning from Brussels. This Friday morning: how EU governments could move to release strategic oil reserves amid US pressure, and the EU closes the book on Ukraine’s $27 billion deficit.

item.title: Over 1,000 adult LEGO fans gathered in Denmark near the toy giant’s birthplace
item.description: LEGO reported a net profit of around €1.15 billion in the first half of this year, up 32% on the same period last year, as toymakers increasingly cater to adults buying toys for themselves.

item.title: 'A powerful buffer': How solar saved the EU €37.4 billion since the war on Iran began
item.description: Europe's solar boom is cushioning households from the crippling costs of gas, as the war on Iran continues to highlight the dangers of fossil fuel reliance.

item.title: Europe Today: EU energy prices soar as Spain's housing decrees face Congress vote
item.description: EU diesel prices hit a record average of €2.24 a litre, as Energy Commissioner Jorgensen warns volatility is here to stay. Spain's Congress votes on two housing decrees, with Sanchez's coalition support in doubt, as Bucharest warns of new hybrid threats from Russia.

item.title: Trump vows to hit Iran 'very hard' if linked to flydubai pilot stabbing attack
item.description: Passengers described rushing the cockpit and a fight for control after the plane suddenly plummeted, losing around 17,000 feet of altitude in the span of a minute, according to the Flightradar24 website.

item.title: Protesters rally outside Dublin stadium over Ireland-Israel match
item.description: Around 200 protesters gathered near Dublin’s Aviva Stadium, calling on Ireland to boycott its upcoming Nations League match against Israel

item.title: New Airstream caravan retreat opens in the UAE’s Hajar Mountains
item.description: Caravan Hatta by Our Habitas overlooks Hatta Dam, and offers wellness experiences, stargazing opportunities and open-fire cooking.

item.title: Where in Europe is data centre hiring growing fastest – and why do these jobs pay more?
item.description: Several European countries have seen a significant rise in data centre job postings in recent months. Euronews Business takes a closer look at the reasons behind the growth, including why these roles offer higher pay.

item.title: South Korea warns of 'further measures' if Ukraine refuses public apology over POW transfer disclosure
item.description: The POWs were captured by Ukrainian forces early last year after being deployed alongside thousands of North Korean troops to support Russia's war against Ukraine.

item.title: Swedish researchers create an ‘AI scientist’ that designs and runs its own experiments
item.description: Swedes created an AI system that can carry out the full scientific process from hypothesis to results interpretation with minimal human input.

item.title: How many birds are killed by offshore wind turbines? Scientists use thermal cameras to find out
item.description: A year-long study has observed millions of birds migrating across the North Sea to measure the threat of offshore wind farms.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 2nd, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 2nd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Four hidden trails with medieval roots in the Eastern Alps
item.description: Celtic tribes, Roman soldiers and medieval knights paved the way in the forests of the Eastern Alps. These trails are still there and can be discovered by history lovers during a sunny autumn weekend.

item.title: New ICE guidance sets tighter rules for vehicles stops, bans officers from high-speed chases, memo reveals
item.description: The new guidance comes as the Trump administration faces mounting criticism over a string of deadly incidents involving ICE officers. The agency downplayed the new measures, insisting they’re mere reminders and that current protocols will continue.

item.title: Rubio unblocks $320 million in military aid to Egypt that had been withheld over human rights concerns
item.description: Top US diplomat Marco Rubio signed off on the waiver but argued that Washington’s concerns over its Middle Eastern ally’s human rights record will remain a point of discussion in full bilateral discussions.

item.title: Two killed, two hospitalised and one missing in medical helicopter crash in California's Catalina island
item.description: The helicopter’s operator confirmed that the two deceased were members of its staff, the pilot flying the helicopter and an onboard nurse. Transport safety officials say an investigation into the crash remains ongoing.

item.title: Brazil launches probe into alleged Trump administration plan to fund far-right causes in the country
item.description: The investigation comes as both Lula and Flavio Bolsonaro prepare to contest each other for what is being described as a consequential election in Brazil, that could shape the developing economy’s forecast and future for decades to come.

item.title: Unamuno and H. G. Wells went to the cinema together: unpublished letter confirms it 90 years on
item.description: Written in 1936 and found in the archive of Salamanca’s Casa-Museo Unamuno, the document confirms the Spanish writer dined with the author of 'The War of the Worlds' before going to the cinema together in London.

item.title: Danish military admits flaws in report about 2025 drone incursions
item.description: In a revised report of the incident at Skrydstrup air base released Thursday, the military admitted that their account might have been mistaken.

item.title: Manchester City not 'above the rules', says Downing Street
item.description: After PM Andy Burnham's - a former mayor of Greater Manchester - admission of his fears that the club's owners might leave because of the investigation into 'creative book-keeping', his spokesperson has issued a clarification.

item.title: Kyrylo Budanov: European security without the US would be ‘very dangerous’
item.description: In an exclusive interview with Euronews, the head of the Ukrainian President's Office warned against a future European security architecture without the US and outlined Kyiv’s vision for deeper defence cooperation with Europe.

item.title: José Sevilla resigns as Unicaja chair and declines to remain at the bank
item.description: José Sevilla will step down as Unicaja chairman in April 2027 after deciding not to seek a new term, but will retain his non-executive role at the Málaga-based bank until then.
